title: LRHE independent claim-adjudication record
description: One record per judge invocation, as the DISPATCHER assembles it: the judge's answer plus the fields only the harness can establish. Reconciled from handoff/2026-07-27-opencode/schema/judge-output.schema.json, which the harness never read -- that copy named the matched label `matched_label_id` while `judge_lrhe.cmd_ingest` reads `label_id`, so a reply valid against the published schema would have been ingested with no label at all and every CONFIRMED verdict would have lost the 1:1 defect matching it exists to establish. `label_id` wins because it is what the code reads; the archived spelling is accepted nowhere.

judge_id.description: `<run_id>|<claim_rid>|<judge_family>`. Supplied by the dispatcher from the assignment row and NEVER echoed by the judge: `JUDGE_PROMPT` does not contain it, so requiring the judge to echo it was unsatisfiable. One grok call refused rather than invent one -- the only honest reply available to it -- while 427 others looked correct solely because the dispatcher overwrote whatever they returned. Correlation belongs to the harness, for the same reason `served_model` does

verdict.description: the archived copy also allowed REFUTED and UNRESOLVED. Both are removed. REFUTED comes from the separate cold-refutation pass and is folded in through exec.jsonl, never asserted by a judge; UNRESOLVED had no consumer -- `VERDICTS` is a three-tuple, so such a reply was counted as unmatched and dropped silently. A judge that cannot decide returns PLAUSIBLE, the interim verdict that moves no headline number

label_id.description: the ground-truth label this claim matches, from the label set supplied in the prompt, or null. The judge is shown the labels, so it always has an answer to give

rationale.description: one sentence. Truncated at 400 by ingest, so anything longer is discarded rather than stored

served_model.description: the model the OMP session record says answered, harvested from the record and not from the reply. `judge_family` is the family that was REQUESTED; without this, a silent provider fallback would leave a judgement attributed to a family that never answered and nothing able to detect it. `cmd_ingest` compares it against the expected selector and drops the whole claim when it does not match or cannot be checked -- one surviving judge is not a majority of two

judge_family.description: optional echo of the requested family; the prompt row is authoritative

tool_calls.description: calls that NAMED a tool, from the session record. Judges declare `tools: []`, so anything above zero means the surface leaked

malformed_tool_calls.description: calls naming no tool, which the runtime rejected. Not a boundary breach

verification_status.description: optional. No judge executes anything, so `not_executed` is the only honest value and the field is not required
